liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tennessee Jed** (3 reviews): Tennessee Jed was a hot surprise opener of the second set, followed by a rocking Cumberland Blues; Opening the second set with Tennessee Jed struck the reviewer as unusual [9][11][14]
- **I Need A Miracle** (2 reviews): I Need A Miracle was hot, and Crazy Fingers was sweet; Miracle features some loosely ensemble singing, and the Crazy Fingers jam is praised [9][18]
- **Drums** (1 review): Post-Drums section has Phil Lesh singing along [18]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Comes A Time was a highlight, and energy surged with Gimme Some Lovin'; Phil and Brent shared a vocal rap near the end [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **DupreeÂs Diamond Blues**: rare: 3 archived performances [21]
- **Gimme Some LovinÂ**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [21]
- **TruckinÂ**: rare: 3 archived performances [21]
- **Good LovinÂ**: rare: 3 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd85-11-16.sbd.18374.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 139 min; rated 3.54/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: The matrix recording sounds really good, though this listener found the performance less impressive than other reviewers did; Recording quality is mixed, shifting from warm to bright throughout, but never bad [12][15]
- **gd1985-11-16.172809.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 143 min [3]
- **gd1985-11-16.148775.fob.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 139 min [5]
- **gd85-11-16.schoeps.barbella.12263.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 18 songs; 142 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [8]. Said about its sound: The Schoeps recording earns three stars for sound quality [13]

## Around the show

- Faith healer Peter Popov held a healing event at the civic center next door the following day [10]
- Reviewer's friend lost his glasses during Cumberland; Peter Popov healed people next to the arena the next afternoon [11]
- Reviewer was inside with about 18,000 other fans and also attended the following weekend's Kaiser shows [17]
- One of the shortest shows the reviewer has heard; the pre-Drums portion runs about 27 minutes, and Kaiser 2/20 was shorter overall [14]
- The show is a bit short with nothing especially unusual pulled out, but the playing was good [15]
- Reviewer ranks this among the year's worst shows, with the band tired from the East Coast fall tour; the next week's Kaiser shows were scorching [16]
- The Kaiser shows the following weekend were better than this one [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-11-16.sbd.18374.sbeok.shnf**: source: Lineage: SBD>CM>C>DAT>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN>WAV>CE2K>CDWAVE>SHNTOOL>mkwACT(seekable) [1]
- **gd1985-11-16.172809.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Bob Menke's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [3]. Also: Bob Menke made the master cassette recording and transfer; Charlie Miller coordinated; two sets of masters were combined [3]
- **gd1985-11-16.148775.fob.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [5]
- **gd85-11-16.schoeps.barbella.12263.sbeok.shnf**: source: Schoeps MK41Âs > PCM > DAT > CDRseeded by Steve Barbella [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1985-11-16 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1985-11-16-backstage-pass/) [22]
